items.item_text: Bachelor's Degree in related area and / or equivalent training
7-9 years Budget, finance, research administration and/or management experience in higher education
1-3 years Advising executives in a CFO or similar role
Demonstrated flexibility, resourcefulness, and creative approaches to unique situations, while understanding the broad institutional context in which they must be addressed.

As part of the divisional senior management team, serves as CFO and manages the fiscal resources of the Research Division in close collaboration with the AVCR and VCR. Advises and participates in resource planning, short and long-range policy development, communications and high level analyses of new program development. Ensures proper accounting structures are in place throughout the Division and in support of research campuswide and assesses the impact of changing circumstances to support short- and long-term strategies. Serves as a campus-wide expert in financial matters, providing expertise and direction to the division and campus business officers on an extensive array of accounts and funds, each governed by unique restrictions and controls. Exercises management authority within delegation for appropriate and sensitive issues related to research administration and operations. Investigates and recommends solutions to a wide range of issues in all areas of campus research operations in coordination with Office of Research leadership and staff. Provides direction to Office of Research administrative staff responsible for budget planning and oversight, financial management, post-award financial services, personnel matters, space and office management, institutional cost share on contracts and grants, income and recharge, all financial accounts held by the division, and fiscal processes, in addition to supporting the AVCR and campus on various special programs and projects. Independently and through subordinates initiates and designs complex analysis and reports for senior administrators in support of the campus mission. Serves as subject matter expert, providing leadership, consultation and guidance to the ORUs and the ARC on budget operations, financial management, and staffing considerations (classifications, equity, etc.). Provides ad hoc assistance on interpretation of policies and makes recommendations regarding best practices. Oversees the Research Division chart of accounts and ensures the integrity of the permanent budget and approved staffing with authorized salary actions and expenditures. Manages the fiscal year-end closeout for the department and division.
Excellent critical and innovative thinking to address complex issues.

In collaboration with the AVCR, coordinates with Human Resources and Academic Personnel to provide direction on implementing the Research Division staff personnel program and academic appointments, including classification, compensation, labor relations, employee relations, training and development, and benefits. Through subordinates, facilitates the appointment process for academic and staff roles in the Research Division, ensuring that procedures are followed and that compensation levels and other incentives are appropriate prior to division approval

Represents the division in leading complex and critical projects requiring cross-organizational collaboration. Serves as a key advisor in the Office of Research and has delegated authority to make commitments and represent the VCR and AVCR interests across the organization. Responds to issues with little or no precedence, resolves issues following consultation and using diplomacy, engaging the AVCR or VCR when appropriate. Decisions made by the CFO directly affect the Research Division and can have organization-wide impact. Participates in leadership transition planning for the Research Division and supports onboarding new leaders and appointees. Interacts with senior management on routine matters of research engagement. Works closely with the leadership in Budget & Planning, Business & Financial services, and other campus financial leaders to plan, develop, strategize, and implement initiatives, policies, and solutions for both campus and the Division. Participates in policy development and interpretation encompassing a wide variety of topics. Recommends policy changes and drafts policy revisions. Participates in the design and implementation of information systems across the campus to improve efficiency and effectiveness in handling administrative processes
Demonstrated understanding of federal and state regulations and financial policies for extramural funding.

Directly supervises professional staff and supervisors, and establishes goals and objectives, assigns duties, evaluates performance, and provides career guidance and professional development opportunities. Provides indirect divisional direction and interim coverage for Research Division MSOs and business officers, and provides one-on-one mentoring to ORU business officers as necessary.

Covered Individuals: A Covered Individual includes anyone designated as Personnel or Students under this Policy who physically access a University Facility or Program in connection with their employment, appointment, or education/training. A person accessing a Healthcare Location as a patient, or an art, athletics, entertainment, or other publicly accessible venue at a Location as a member of the public, is not a Covered Individual.
Demonstrated ability to address a wide variety of complex issues which affect the campus and which frequently have no precedent.
Thorough knowledge of financial/budgetary/accounting policies, practices, and systems.
Demonstrated consulting, relationship building and strategic thinking skills.
Proven ability to use tools and software to perform complex financial analysis, management, and reporting.
Strong interpersonal skills and demonstrated ability to build and work successfully in teams.
Exceptional communication skills. Management, leadership, and coaching skills to create and foster effective working relationships, both internal and external to the VCR immediate office.
Extraordinary sensitivity to constituents and ability to respond to situations with tact, compassion, and diplomacy.
